summary: Today’s pulse tracks AstraZeneca shares plunge over talks with US cancer drug firm on $400bn merger, Paris prosecutor investigates alleged bullying in government departments after suicide attempt, and Kmart sells out of low-cost rival to Meta camera glasses across Australia amid warnings of ‘privacy nightmare’. Across Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are jones, monday, and radio. In the background, Most Sydney road tolls to keep rising after Transurban accused of blocking reforms and Alan Jones argues ‘rivalry’ and ‘treachery’ but after decades wielding the sword of public opinion, he’s the one on trial keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: AstraZeneca shares plunge over talks with US cancer drug firm on $400bn merger
headlines.description: Bristol Myers Squibb tie-up would create world’s fourth largest drugmaker but analysts question rationale for deal More than £15bn was wiped off the value of Britain’s biggest drugmaker, AstraZeneca, on Monday after a report that it was in discussions to take over its US rival Bristol Myers Squibb in a deal that would create a near $400bn (£300bn) pharmaceutical group. AstraZeneca, run by Pascal Soriot, its longtime chief executive, is the second biggest listed company in the UK, with a market value of nearly £196bn before the news broke. BMS, headquartered in Princeton, New Jersey, and known for its cancer treatments, is worth $133bn.

headlines.title: Paris prosecutor investigates alleged bullying in government departments after suicide attempt
headlines.description: Internal inquiries also opened after two suicides and two attempted suicides of staff in departments connected to PM’s office The Paris state prosecutor has opened a preliminary inquiry into alleged workplace bullying after the attempted suicide of a staff member in a department connected to the French prime minister’s office, France Inter radio has revealed. The public radio station reported on Monday that two government workers in different departments had ended their lives in the past year, and two others had attempted suicide. The radio station said complaints of alleged workplace bullying had been made.

headlines.title: Kmart sells out of low-cost rival to Meta camera glasses across Australia amid warnings of ‘privacy nightmare’
headlines.description: Expert says people face being filmed without their consent as $89 Anko smartglasses sell out in stores and online As of Monday, the clear-lens, black-rimmed glasses, which can capture images and record high-definition videos, were sold out at Kmart stores across Australia and online.

headlines.title: Most Sydney road tolls to keep rising after Transurban accused of blocking reforms
headlines.description: Handful of tollroads to get one-off price cuts but WestConnex toll to keep rising at least 4% a year Only a handful of Sydney’s motorways will receive one-off toll cuts under a deal announced by the state Labor government on Monday, as the tolling bill footed by taxpayers surpasses $1bn.

headlines.title: Alan Jones argues ‘rivalry’ and ‘treachery’ but after decades wielding the sword of public opinion, he’s the one on trial
headlines.description: His legal strategy was apparent from the very first. Jones will, it was explicitly stated, seek to undermine the ‘credibility and reliability’ of his accusers The booming voice, the vast radio audience, the bully pulpit of an eponymous TV show, the great and the good on speed-dial, a staffer in the prime ministerial office dubbed the “minister for Alan Jones”: these were not ancillaries peripheral to the Jones empire, they were central to it.

headlines.title: South-eastern Europe faces heatwave energy crunch as Romania detonates Danube rock to increase water flow – Europe live
headlines.description: Explosives used to move a large rock and let more water flow to cool nuclear power plant More must be done ⁠to strengthen the European Union’s borders at critical points, ⁠European Commission president ⁠Ursula ​von der Leyen told Spanish prime minister Pedro Sánchez ⁠in a letter. In the carefully-calibrated letter, first reported by Reuters and a number of Spanish media, von der Leyen was quoted as congratulating Spain for swiftly handling the incident and “successfully preventing” the onward migration to mainland Spain and the EU.

headlinePool.title: Sunday Times and Sun columnist Rod Liddle dies aged 66
headlinePool.description: Tributes paid across industry to provocative journalist who died after short illness Writer and broadcaster Rod Liddle, a prominent columnist for the Sunday Times and the Sun, has died after a short illness. Liddle, whose provocative style attracted both praise and criticism, also wrote for the Spectator magazine and earlier in his career edited BBC Radio 4’s Today programme. He was 66.

headlinePool.title: Holdouts for Trump’s attorney general pick say they will advance his nomination to the full Senate – US politics live
headlinePool.description: Republican senators John Cornyn and Thom Tillis say that formal order withdrawing ‘anti-weaponization fund’ has addressed their concerns Blanche formally rescinds Trump’s $1.8bn ‘anti-weaponization fund’ The most closely watched competition is the Democratic primary for the US Senate, where congresswoman Haley Stevens is up against former public health official Abdul El-Sayed . They’re vying to ultimately win the seat of outgoing senator Gary Peters in November. The race has now turned into a proxy battle for the future of the Democratic party. Establishment-backed Stevens has received support from party leaders and her race has been buoyed by millions from the pro-Israel lobby. Meanwhile the insurgent El-Sayed has built a strong grassroots movement and is endorsed by progressives lawmakers in the Democratic caucus.

headlinePool.title: Romania blasts rock to divert water from drought-hit Danube to nuclear reactor
headlinePool.description: Hungary and Romania face energy crisis as record-low river levels force atomic power plants to reduce output Europe live – latest updates Romanian naval forces carried out a controlled explosion to help redirect vital cooling water from the drought-hit Danube to the country’s last working nuclear ⁠reactor, as neighbouring Hungary ​said it may be able to eke out two more days of power from its only atomic plant. Hungary and Romania have been forced to shut down nuclear reactors cooled by the Danube for the first time, as record-low water levels deepen fears of an energy crisis across the region. Romania has declared a nationwide state of emergency throughout August stemming from a decline in electricity production after record low Danube river levels led to the shutdown at the Cernavodǎ nuclear plant.

headlinePool.title: Rhine falls to record low levels as drought strains Europe's rivers
headlinePool.description: Low water levels in the Rhine, Danube and Po have curtailed the transport of goods and reduced electricity output.

headlinePool.title: Restore leader accuses Farage of ‘outright lying’ over pact offer but says his party ‘remains open’ – UK politics live
headlinePool.description: Rupert Lowe says no talks have taken place after the Reform UK leader said he was ‘open to conversation’ on some sort of electoral deal Zia Yusuf said under the plan Reform will create an “integrated surveillance command”, which he claims will “unify” military and intelligence surveillance, making “ours the most surveilled maritime border in the world”. “Any vessel attempting to cross illegally will be intercepted by our armed forces who will return them back to France,” he said, adding that emergency legislation would be given to the armed forces to equip them with the “necessary powers”.

headlinePool.title: Middle East crisis live: Iran denies Trump’s claims that talks due to take place
headlinePool.description: Iranian spokesperson says there are no plans to receive or send a delegation following US president’s assertion that talks would take place on Monday Iran in talks with Oman over shipping route but not US, says Tehran People walk near a billboard depicting Iran’s late supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, on a street in Tehran, Iran, earlier today. Six Saudi-flagged supertankers have changed course in the Gulf of Aden in recent days amid threats from the Iran-aligned Houthis , Reuters reports.

headlinePool.title: Washington wildfires destroy homes, force thousands to evacuate
headlinePool.description: Spokane Mayor Lisa Brown says nearly half of the city's neighborhoods have either been evacuated or are at risk as the fires remain uncontained.

headlinePool.title: Aung San Suu Kyi appears healthy in first confirmed outside contact for 2.5 years
headlinePool.description: Photos newly released by Myanmar's military government show Suu Kyi meeting with an ICRC official.

headlinePool.title: Iran says it is in talks with Oman but not the US after Trump says negotiations to resume
headlinePool.description: Tehran has repeatedly closed off the strait since the US and Israel attacked the country in February.
